_readme: Example routing config for the Fluxion provider gateway.
Copy to config/provider_routes.json and edit. That path is gitignored: it
names local workspace paths and is specific to one machine. `fluxion-provider
init` writes a minimal version of this file and never overwrites an existing
one, so editing in place is safe.
JSON has no comments, so notes live in `_`-prefixed keys. The loader ignores
unknown keys everywhere except `routes`, whose keys are role names.
Validate any edit with: fluxion-provider doctor
The rationale behind each field lives in the module docstrings under
src/fluxion/provider_gateway/ — start with config.py and local_agent.py.

_comment: A local agent: Fluxion runs an agent CLI on your own subscription and
renders its output as a model response. No API key, no per-token charge.
`executor` names a Fluxion executor: claude, codex, or antigravity.
Capability flags are granted automatically for local agents, so only
_default_workspace: Where the agent runs when a request carries no workspace. Codex normally
reports its git repo root, so this is only a fallback. Leave it empty to
have such requests refused: guessing points an agent at the wrong
repository, and it starts editing before anyone notices.

_comment: A second local agent on a different CLI. Useful for review: a reviewer
backed by a different vendor than the worker will not repeat the worker's
A third CLI. `antigravity` cannot run read-only, so routing a read-only
role (explorer, reviewer) here is refused rather than run with write
Its value is as a reviewer of a *different* vendor's work: Gemini reading
code Claude wrote catches what Claude cannot see in itself.

_policies_note: A policy is a named strategy: an ordered candidate list plus optional
`fallback` entries are tried after `candidates`, in order. Order is also the
tie-break, so two equally-scored models always resolve the same way across
Weight dimensions: quality, cost, latency, quota. An unknown name is a load
error rather than a silently ignored typo.
_routes_note: Role -> policy. Roles arrive as the X-Fluxion-Route header, one per Codex
This object takes no `_`-prefixed notes: every key here is treated as a role
name and every value must name a defined policy.
